Subject: Post-call: Proof-of-Fit plan and next actions for hosting vs dedicated vs private

Hi Jon / Sasha —

Thanks again for the deep call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can align on the right deployment mode for Vestra's patient-notification pipeline: Hosted API (fastest to prod), Dedicated capacity (predictable throughput & isolation), or Private VPC (full network control / compliance).

Key items from our call:
- Traffic profile: ~120k short messages/day, 80% sub-128 tokens, peak bursts up to 200rps for 2–3 hours/day.
- Data sensitivity: PHI is present in a subset of notifications; encryption at rest + KMS required.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 250ms for 90% of requests during peaks.
- Success criteria for a 3-week Proof-of-Fit (PoF):
  - Achieve p95 latency <= 250ms under a 150rps simulated mix with 90% of tokens under 128 tokens.
  - Validation of KMS integration and audit log access.
  - End-to-end end-user cost estimate (tokens + infra) with 10% margin.
  - Clear rollback plan if model quality drift > 5% on the provided eval set.

Proposed PoF approach (attached: redwood-proof-of-fit-plan.xlsx):
1) Week 0 (this week): finalize scope & confirm dataset for quality checks; pick target route (we recommend starting on Hosted API to prove quality + latency quickly, then run Dedicated capacity head-to-head for cost/throughput).
2) Week 1: baseline runs on Hosted -> collect latency/cost/quality telemetry.
3) Week 2: Dedicated capacity run with same traffic profile; compare unit economics and average latency under load.
4) Week 3: If required for compliance, spin an isolated Private VPC dry-run to validate KMS/HSM and networking (this is typically longer; aim for at least a narrow smoke test in PoF).

Requested from Vestra to proceed:
- Confirm which sample payloads we should run (anonymized).
- Point of contact for KMS/infosec (SLA for creds & firewall windows).
- A 60-minute technical dry-run slot next Tuesday for Vivek to test a traffic replay.

Next steps / owners:
- Vestra: confirm sample set & security contact (Jon) — by EOD Thursday 11/2.
- Redwood: prepare hosted baseline and Dedicated capacity config; share estimated costs — owner: Ava (deliver by Monday 11/6).
- Redwood infra: Vivek will schedule the tech dry-run once credentials are available.

Attachment: redwood-proof-of-fit-plan.xlsx (summary, test matrix, runbook). Also attached: sow-template-v1.docx (for contracting milestones if you want 30-day reserved Dedicated).

Happy to hop on a 15-min alignment call if that helps.

Best,
Ava Chen
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Jon / Ava — short technical notes after reviewing the PoF sheet: 

1) For the Hosted baseline: we can simulate the 150rps burst with continuous batching enabled; expected p95 for model X-small is ~180–220ms in our stage cluster (assuming token distribution you shared). We'll capture p50/p90/p95 during the run.
2) For Dedicated run: recommend reserved pool with 2x capacity headroom to emulate headroom from customer-run spikes — that maps to a 2-GPU pool for the workload profile. I will produce an infra-estimate (hours + infra cost delta) and a Private VPC smoke-test checklist.
3) Security/compliance: for KMS integration we need a KMS IAM role and a short-lived service account. Sasha: if you can open a ticket to your infra team to allow the role creation and a firewall exception for the dry-run window that will speed the smoke test.

Blockers / risks:
- Private VPC full validation will likely push past the 3-week PoF if we need network approvals and on-prem firewall changes. Recommend we treat Private VPC as a gated follow-up: do Hosted & Dedicated first, then run a targeted Private VPC smoke validation once procurement/security windows are open.

I'll upload the infra runbook to the Drive folder and tag the sections with required inputs.
